title: Paying the hostel fee: a sequence diagram
instructions:
## Objects talking in time

When a student pays the hostel fee through the portal: the **Student** sends `payFee(amount)` to the **Portal**; the Portal sends `charge(amount)` to the **MobileMoney** service; if the charge succeeds the service returns `ok` and the Portal sends `confirmBooking()` to the **BookingService** and returns a `receipt` to the Student; if it fails the service returns `declined` and the Portal returns `error` to the Student.

## Do this

Write the sequence diagram with four participants, the messages in order, and an `alt` fragment with the success and failure branches (`alt success` … `else declined` … `end`). Synchronous calls are `->>`, returns are `-->>`.

config.starter:
diagram: sequence
participant Student
participant Portal

initialState.source:
diagram: sequence
participant Student
participant Portal

hints: Student ->> Portal : payFee(amount) is the first message.
The alt fragment wraps the two outcomes: alt success / else declined / end.
Returns are dashed: MobileMoney -->> Portal : ok

checks.label: payFee, then charge, then ok, then confirmBooking, then receipt
The failure branch: declined, then error
The Portal charges the mobile money service
The receipt returns to the Student

realityNote: Sequence diagrams are where timeouts and retries become visible: what happens if the mobile money provider never answers? Real payment integrations add an idempotency key to charge() so a retried call cannot charge twice.
